description.value: The study examined cerebral responses in healthy normal-weight women while viewing photographs of high-calorie foods, low-calorie foods, and nonedible dining-related utensils, focusing on food-related and calorie-specific motivational salience.

design.value: Functional MRI study of 13 healthy right-handed women using three separate visual activation runs with alternating 30-second task and control blocks; stimulus order was counterbalanced across subjects.

name.value: internet based resource for determining the caloric content of foods (www.freeweightlosscenter.com)

description.value: Each recognition test presented previously seen category-specific photographs randomly intermixed with novel distractor photographs; subjects indicated whether each photograph had been seen previously.
Subjects rated how each photo affected their appetite on an 11-point scale ranging from −5, highly aversive, to +5, highly appealing.
Questionnaire regarding hourly dietary intake over the preceding day; calorie intake for the 6 h prior to the scan was calculated by two independent raters.

source_definition.value: low-calorie food, high-calorie food, and utensil conditions relative to control conditions
foods that differ according to caloric content
defined operationally by the objective ratings of the appetitive appeal of the food categories

description.value: 13 healthy right-handed female participants with no history of eating disorder, psychiatric diagnoses, or neurologic illness, recruited from the staff of McLean Hospital.

recruitment_method.value: recruited from the staff of McLean Hospital

task_description.value: Three visual activation tasks were presented over separate scanning runs: low-calorie foods, high-calorie foods, and nonedible food-related utensils. Each paradigm consisted of two 30-sec stimulation periods alternating with three control blocks of equal duration.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to view each series of photographs and to try to remember them for a recognition test upon completion of the scanning session.

stimuli.value: Professional quality full-color photographs of low-calorie foods, high-calorie foods, food-related utensils, and visually interesting nonfood control objects.

task_performance_measures.value: percentage of items correctly recognized during the posttest

instrument.value: 1.5-T GE LX MRI scanner equipped with a quadrature RF head coil

description.value: BOLD activation data were acquired during three 50-scan runs, each consisting of five alternating 30-s control/task periods. Three dummy images were taken at the outset of each functional scan.
Matched T1-weighted high-resolution images were collected for every subject at the beginning of the scanning session.
Functional images were corrected for motion, convolved into three-dimensional space, smoothed, and resliced to 2 × 2 × 2 mm within stereotaxic space.

steps.value: motion correction using an intrarun realignment algorithm with the first image as reference
isotropic Gaussian smoothing with FWHM = 10 mm
reslicing to 2 × 2 × 2 mm within stereotaxic space using sinc interpolation

model_settings.value: A statistical parametric map was generated for each subject; fixed-effects group SPM contrast maps were created for the low-calorie food, high-calorie food, and utensil conditions relative to control conditions. Group SPMs and all contrasts used P < .005 uncorrected with a minimum cluster size of 20 contiguous voxels; the high-calorie condition also used a post hoc threshold of P < .0005 uncorrected.

description.value: Photographs depicting freshly prepared garden salads, whole-grain cereals, fresh vegetables, and fruits.
Photographs such as french fries, ice cream sundaes, cheeseburgers, hot dogs, chocolate chip cookies, barbequed chicken, strawberry shortcake, and pasta with meat sauce.
Photographs of forks and spoons, dishes, placemats, chopsticks, and tableware, with no edible items present.
Photographs of visually interesting objects that are generally not consumed as food in modern western cultures, such as rocks, shrubs, bricks, trees, and flowers.
